2026-08-14T12:32:17.5153416Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5153805Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5154132Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5154607Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5155052Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5156792Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5158435Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5160157Z >
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5162422Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5164772Z >
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5166128Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5167018Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5167237Z ### How to Use
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5167497Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5168232Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5169307Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5169495Z ```bash
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5170046Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5170905Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5171508Z ```
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5171711Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5171978Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5172496Z ```bash
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5173027Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5174684Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5175850Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5176592Z ```
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5176800Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5177471Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5178325Z ```bash
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5178884Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5179868Z ```
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5180096Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5180442Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5181213Z ```bash
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5181746Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5182601Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5183301Z ```
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5183505Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5183767Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5184183Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5185799Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5187350Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5187533Z ```bash
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5187982Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5188920Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5189729Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5190037Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5190519Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5193871Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5194704Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5195362Z ```
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5195578Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5196326Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5197219Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5197395Z ```bash
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5198121Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5199014Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5199714Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5200132Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5200531Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5201335Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5201872Z ```
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5202069Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5202279Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5203077Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5204039Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5204996Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5206153Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5207261Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5207788Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5207966Z ### Notes
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5208171Z 
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5208790Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5210185Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5211421Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5212744Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5213937Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5215042Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5216175Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-14T12:32:17.5216859Z </mcp-clis>
